identity.title: CVE-2026-132257
identity.description: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. identity.title: CVE-2026-134056

identity.title: CVE-2026-134848
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not refuse a NUL character in a startup parameter. The StartupMessage is a list of NUL-terminated strings, so a NUL in the database name, user, currentSchema, options or ApplicationName adds further parameters. %00 in a URL decodes to a NUL. Someone who controls part of the URL or a property can choose another login role or add replication=database, although the connection still has to pass the authentication of that role. On a server that trusts the client, the attacker can log in as any role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: NONE, user interaction: NONE

cwe_names.CWE-158: Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character

_relevance.reason: Widely deployed PostgreSQL JDBC driver vulnerability allowing role assumption and authentication bypass on trusting servers.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134844
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, uses unqualified operators and functions in the catalog queries of DatabaseMetaData, ResultSetMetaData and TypeInfoCache. A role with CREATE on a schema of the application's search_path can add an operator with an exact type match, and the server runs it with the privileges of the application's role. TypeInfoCache also resolves an unqualified type name such as interval by its own ranking. A domain with that name in another schema, even the temporary schema of another session, can be used instead, and its CHECK runs in the application's session. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: Privilege escalation in widely deployed PostgreSQL JDBC driver via unqualified catalog queries.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134845
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not enforce TLS for some settings that ask for it. When sslmode is not set, an ssl value such as 1, on, yes or verify-full gives sslmode=prefer, or no TLS before 42.2.5. A service given in the Properties instead of the URL is ignored, so the sslmode of its pg_service.conf entry is lost. BaseDataSource.setUrl() keeps an sslmode, channelBinding or gssEncMode that was set before it. An attacker on the network path can then read and change the traffic. Versions 9.4.1208 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: NONE, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: TLS enforcement failure in widely deployed PostgreSQL JDBC driver enabling network traffic interception.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134843
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not close the connection when an unchecked exception interrupts a request. Part of a Bind message stays in the send buffer, and the server reads the bytes that follow as the rest of it. The bytes of a value uploaded later on the same connection can then run as a SQL command. Since 42.6.0 a setBinaryStream() value without a length that is executed again throws such an exception, as does the driver's own retry after SQLState 0A000 or 26000. An application stream that throws an unchecked exception has the same effect in all versions. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134841
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, misreads some quoted text in its query parser. A `}` inside a literal ends a JDBC escape such as `{ts}`, and the rest of the literal is translated as SQL. A dollar quote whose tag has a non-ASCII symbol or space is not recognized. An `E''` string with a doubled quote is scanned as a standard string. `{fn right}` and `{fn timestampdiff}` with a negative argument produce a `--` comment. In each case text that the application quoted correctly can run as SQL with the privileges of the application's database role. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: NONE, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: SQL injection via query parser misinterpretation in widely deployed PostgreSQL JDBC driver.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134842
identity.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, can quote a string parameter for the wrong value of standard_conforming_strings when preferQueryMode=simple is set. Before 42.7.6 any session with the setting off was affected. The statement cache can also reuse a parse made under the other setting. With allowEncodingChanges=true and the EUC_JP or SJIS client encoding, the yen sign acts as a backslash. All versions before 42.7.15 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

identity.title: CVE-2026-135258
identity.description:
MISP contains multiple related authorization and input-validation flaws in its object editing and attachment handling workflows.

- A user with permission to edit their own object could inject a foreign attribute identifier into the object revision form. The revision data, stored in the server-side session, was merged into the stored object before the save diff was computed. The save then wrote to the foreign attribute row by its identifier without verifying that the row belonged to the caller's event or organisation, allowing an attacker to overwrite or soft-delete an attribute in another organisation's private event.
- Attachment file paths were constructed directly from event and attribute identifiers supplied by the request. Because no type or format validation was applied, crafted values (for example directory-traversal sequences or file-name extensions) could cause the application to read from or write to file-system locations outside the intended attachment directory.
- The audit-log behaviour recorded an edit under the event identifier carried in the save payload rather than the event identifier of the stored database row. An attacker who included a different event identifier in the save could cause the audit entry to be attributed to the wrong event, undermining the integrity of the audit trail.

Exploitation requires an authenticated web-session user with object-editing permissions (perm_add / perm_modify). API-key-only requests do not carry the PHP session and are not affected by the revision-session vector.

Affected versions: MISP < 2.5.52. Fixed in 2.5.52.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

cwe_names.CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

_relevance.reason: Authorization bypass in MISP threat intelligence platform enabling cross-organization data manipulation, fitting government and critical infrastructure deployment footprint.

identity.title: CVE-2026-135256
identity.description:
MISP contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in its Warninglist feature. Warninglist entries of type "regex" are evaluated against attribute values without any backtracking limit. An authenticated user with permission to add or import warninglist entries can supply a crafted regular expression pattern that triggers excessive backtracking in the PCRE engine, causing sustained CPU consumption and denial of service.

Additionally, imported warninglists were not validated for syntactic correctness before replacing existing entries, allowing malformed or malicious patterns to be persisted and later evaluated without prior rejection.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with the ability to create, edit, or import warninglist entries (users below site-admin level can add entries).
- The target MISP instance has at least one warninglist of type "regex" that will be evaluated against incoming attribute values.

Impact:
- Sustained CPU exhaustion leading to denial of service for all users of the MISP instance.
- Potential for cascading performance degradation on shared infrastructure.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: ReDoS DoS in MISP threat intelligence platform; widely deployed in government and enterprise cyber defense infrastructure.

identity.title: CVE-2026-135252
identity.description:
MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION option was enabled by default, causing the library to automatically follow HTTP redirects without the application's own per-hop validation logic being invoked.

- Feed requests: MISP implements its own redirect validation for feed sources, but libcurl was following redirects before that validation could execute, allowing a malicious or compromised feed source to redirect the request to arbitrary internal URLs.
- Sync requests: Sync peers are server-configured, and the application does not perform per-hop redirect validation for sync traffic. libcurl's automatic redirect following allowed a malicious sync peer to redirect the request to internal network resources.

An attacker who is a configured sync peer, controls a feed source URL, or can influence DNS resolution for a configured endpoint can exploit this to cause the MISP server to issue requests to arbitrary internal services, potentially reading sensitive data or interacting with internal APIs that are not otherwise exposed.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

cwe_names.CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

_relevance.reason: SSRF in MISP feed/sync handling bypasses redirect validation; critical flaw in widely deployed threat intelligence infrastructure.

identity.title: CVE-2026-135250
identity.description:
MISP contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its image processing pipeline. When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application decodes user-supplied image data using the GD library without first validating the declared pixel dimensions in the image header.

Because GD allocates its pixel buffers outside the scope of PHP's memory_limit directive, a crafted image with an extremely large declared resolution (for example, 20000 x 20000 pixels) can trigger a multi-gigabyte memory allocation during the decode step, exhausting available system memory and causing the PHP worker process or the host to become unresponsive.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated MISP user with permission to upload attachments or to create/view event graphs.
- The ability to supply a crafted image file (e.g., a PNG with a valid header declaring oversized dimensions).

Impact:
- Denial of service: memory exhaustion leading to process crash or host unavailability.
- No confidentiality or integrity impact is indicated by the evidence.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: Authenticated memory exhaustion DoS in MISP image processing; impacts widely deployed threat intelligence sharing infrastructure.

Brotli and zstd, with their high compression ratios, made the attack particularly effective.

The vulnerability required no authentication and no special conditions beyond the ability to send an HTTP request with a Content-Encoding header. The impact is a complete loss of availability for the affected MISP instance.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

identity.title: CVE-2026-135239
identity.description:
MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a site admin could create or import records attributed to an organisation other than their own, or cause the creation of a new organisation from a payload-supplied identifier.

The root cause is an inconsistent authorization check: the code validated one representation of the creator organisation (for example a numeric ID or a UUID field) while storing a different representation taken directly from the user-supplied payload. In the event import path, a MISP export naming another organisation or a fabricated one was accepted and stored under that organisation. In the galaxy, cluster, analyst data, and sighting capture paths, the nested organisation object from the payload was used to create or reference an organisation without verifying the caller's membership.

Impact:
- Data (events, galaxies, clusters, analyst notes, sightings) can be created under an organisation the attacker does not belong to, polluting that organisation's data and potentially exposing it to that organisation's members.
- New organisations can be created from attacker-supplied identifiers, introducing phantom entities into the MISP instance.
- The integrity of the threat-intelligence data store is compromised because attribution is no longer trustworthy.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: Authorization bypass allowing cross-organization data attribution in MISP; impacts multi-tenant threat intelligence sharing infrastructure.

identity.title: CVE-2026-93585
identity.description:
An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows endpoint with LocalSystem privileges. The affected agent service does not sufficiently enforce authorization restrictions for certain privileged remote management operations. Under specific conditions, the agent fails to apply the intended user impersonation mechanism and executes user-supplied commands within the security context of the agent service, which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

As a result, an authenticated attacker may bypass the intended privilege restrictions and execute arbitrary commands with the highest user-mode privileges on an affected Windows system. Successful exploitation may lead to complete compromise of the affected endpoint, including unauthorized access to sensitive information, modification of system configurations, installation of malicious software, or disruption of system availability. 

The vulnerability does not require administrative credentials or user interaction after successful authentication.

identity.title: CVE-2026-86312
identity.description:
Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could carry out more than a simple health check. In deployments that rely on Solr's rule-based authorization, a client granted only the low-privilege health permission could thereby trigger behavior that should require higher privileges; where the shipped security.json template leaves the health permission unauthenticated, no credentials are required at all. 


This issue affects Apache Solr from 9.0.0 through the releases preceding the fixed versions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.11.0 or 10.1.0, which resolve the issue.




You are affected if you run an affected version and allow the /admin/ping endpoint to be reached with only the health permission. This includes the default sample security configuration installed by the bin/solr CLI, where that endpoint is unauthenticated.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict access to the /admin/ping endpoint in their authorization configuration — for example by requiring a trusted role for that path — and ensure Solr is not reachable from untrusted clients or networks, as recommended for all Solr deployments.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: Apache Solr authorization bypass on default unauthenticated ping endpoint in widely deployed enterprise search platform.

identity.title: CVE-2026-93584
identity.description:
An SQL injection vulnerability in OTRS versions 2024.3.1 through 2026.8.1 allows unauthenticated remote attackers to inject arbitrary SQL expressions through the Survey endpoint.

The vulnerability exists in the Kernel::System::Survey::Request::RequestGet() method, which directly incorporates an attacker-controlled survey key into a SQL query without using parameterized statements. Successful exploitation allows attackers to retrieve ticket information and perform boolean-based or time-based blind SQL injection to extract potentially sensitive data accessible to the OTRS database account. Exploitation does not require authentication, a valid survey key, or an existing survey request. The external frontend must be accessible.

identity.title: CVE-2026-121456
identity.description:
A privilege escalation vulnerability in the Axivion Suite ApiToken permission restriction for OIDC and SAML users of the Axivion Dashboard. 
When a user creates an ApiToken with a restricted token type (for example, IDE plugin or Continuous Integration), some of that user’s permissions should be removed from the token. For users who sign in to the Dashboard through OIDC, or through the SAML preview feature, this restriction has no effect. Exploitability is low: an attacker needs an ApiToken that has been leaked, or one that was shared on the assumption that its permissions were restricted.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: LOW, user interaction: ACTIVE

_relevance.reason: OIDC and SAML token permission bypass in Axivion Suite CI/CD platform, directly affecting identity and access control mechanisms.

identity.title: CVE-2026-134850
identity.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in aceberg WatchYourLAN up to 2.1.4. Affected by this issue is the function getPortState of the file backend/internal/api/api-network.go of the component Web API. The manipulation of the argument addr leads to server-side request forgery. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
